decision.exceedance_rule: any defined tract with inclusive selected edge share > 0.15 (more than 5 percentage points above nominal 10%)
decision.selection_rank_direction_finding: Frozen T4 uses descending accumulation with rank ceil(n*(1-top_fraction)); this is a rank-direction mismatch for a top-decile selector and explains the widespread high selected shares. Tie expansion is also fully accounted for, but should not be conflated with this rank-direction issue.
decision.threshold_excess_definition: inclusive selected edge count / total tract-edge segments - nominal top_fraction

recipe.current_threshold_rule: rank=max(1,ceil(total_edges*(1-top_fraction))) in descending-score accumulation; select every tract-edge segment whose integer degree product is >= threshold
recipe.delta_sign: inclusive T4 gap minus exact fractional-boundary gap
recipe.fractional_rule: select exactly total_edges*top_fraction; take all score groups above the boundary and uniform fractional edge mass from the boundary tie group, applying the same fraction to its all/non-named lengths
recipe.gap_rule: non-named clipped length / all clipped length among selected tract-edge segments
recipe.quantile_method: linear interpolation at (n-1)*p over defined tracts
recipe.rank_direction_finding: The frozen implementation accumulates from highest to lowest but uses rank ceil(n*(1-top_fraction)); with top_fraction=0.1 this selects roughly the top 90% before tie expansion, not a top decile. Therefore observed excess is not attributable to ties alone. This audit leaves the candidate implementation unchanged.
recipe.weight: degree(u) * degree(v), where endpoint connector incidence is counted over eligible provided roads
